term: translation-covariant absolute selection from relative data
definition: A deterministic function takes signed relative-displacement data to a labeled absolute configuration. Covariance demands that translating the input configuration by any real displacement translate that output by the same displacement. Because the input data are translation-invariant, this norm is incompatible with an inhabited absolute output.
note: Explicit analyst norm, not equivalent to sufficient reason as such, all explanation, divine choice or gauge equivalence. An enriched asymmetric input or rejection of covariance escapes the displayed obstruction; origin normalization is translation-invariant rather than covariant.
